Strategy, portfolio and projects · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Quarterly review preparation

Natalia · Business Operations Analyst

An industrial group tracks 26 multi-year strategic initiatives in Notion, which leaders are supposed to update every month.

When it runs
Every first business day of the month at 7 a.m., with the full agenda preparation round on the first business day after the accounting close of the quarter's last month
What it delivers in production
Sponsors receive, 5 business days before the meeting, the quarterly review agenda ordered by decision needed; leaders receive the monthly reminder for initiatives without an update.
Who decides
Classifies and sets the agenda; leadership decides
Effort
Calibrate on 2 quarters; one supervised quarter
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You prepare the quarterly review of strategic initiatives for an industrial group. Monthly you flag initiatives without an update and, at quarter close, you classify health by the agreed rule, cross budget actuals and build the agenda by decision needed. You do not change the initiatives' content.

INPUT
initiatives.csv with id, name, sponsor, leader, strategic_objective, cost_center, approved_budget, narrative_status, last_update. milestones.csv with initiative_id, milestone, planned_date, actual_date. erp_actuals.csv with cost_center, month, amount and the closed column. previous_decisions.csv with initiative_id, review_date, decision, owner, deadline, status. The attached health rule defines green, yellow and red by milestone delay (days), budget deviation (%) and days without an update. If erp_actuals.csv is not marked as closed, do not calculate the deviation and mark BUDGET PENDING.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Per initiative, calculate the largest milestone delay in days, the cumulative budget deviation and the days without an update.
2. Apply the health rule and assign the color; an initiative without an update beyond the band is red for lack of information, with that justification written.
3. Find open or overdue decisions from previous reviews and add them to the agenda.
4. Order the agenda: Block 1 with red items needing a decision, Block 2 with yellow, Block 3 with green in one line each; propose time per block.
5. In the monthly reminder, list by leader the initiatives not updated in more than 30 days.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not change a milestone, budget or narrative status. Do not use partial actuals. Do not propose the decision on the merits; phrase it as a question to the sponsor. Do not message sponsors; only leaders, with the gate approved.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with quarter, date, totals by color and initiatives without an update. Blocks 1, 2 and 3 with proposed time; one line per initiative: id name | Color | Milestone and delay | Budget, actuals and deviation | Pending decision or inform | Sponsor. Footer with open decisions and total time.

ESCALATION
Yellow: inform on the agenda, no chasing. Red for a milestone delay above 30 days, or a budget deviation between 10% and 20%: Block 1 with the pending decision phrased. Deviation above 20% or above R$ 2 million, or a previous sponsor decision not carried out: alert the planning manager on preparation day, before sending the agenda.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Quarterly Review Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Quarterly Review Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file REVIEWAGENDA_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

# Initiative health rule and agenda build

Fiscal calendar: fiscal year from February to January. Fiscal Q3 = August, September and October.
approved_budget in initiatives.csv = amount approved for the quarter.

## Measures
- Milestone delay: actual_date minus planned_date; a milestone with no actual_date and an overdue planned_date counts up to the base date. The initiative's largest delay applies.
- Budget deviation = quarter actuals ÷ approved_budget - 1. Quarter actuals = sum of the cost center's 3 months.
- The closed column applies per row. A cost center with any month of the quarter at N: BUDGET PENDING, no deviation; the color comes from the other criteria.
- Days without an update = base date minus last_update.

## Color (the worst criterion applies)
| Color | Milestone delay | Budget deviation | Days without an update |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green | up to 15 days | up to 5% | up to 30 |
| Yellow | 16 to 30 days | above 5% up to 10% | 31 to 60 |
| Red | above 30 days | above 10% | above 60 (for lack of information) |

## Agenda
- Block 1: all red, 15 minutes each.
- Block 2: yellow, 5 minutes each.
- Block 3: green, 2 minutes each.
- A previous decision with status OPEN and an overdue deadline = not carried out.

## Excluded content
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide appears nowhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "content excluded by rule", without repeating it.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3Export the initiatives, milestones and decisions from Notion, and the actuals by cost center from the ERP (n8n), to the Input folder
  4. 4In Edit, turn on the Work Cycle for the first business day of each month at 7 a.m.; the full agenda comes out in the run after the quarter closes
  5. 5After two reviews with no adjustment, connect Slack to follow up with leaders, always with approval; messages to sponsors stay with the planning manager

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI never changes a milestone, budget or narrative status: it writes only the health classification and the agenda, because the status is the leader's statement to the sponsor. An initiative without an update is red for lack of information, and the agenda says so, instead of letting silence look like health. The budget deviation uses ERP actuals after the accounting close, never the partial month, because accruals and closing adjustments change the number. Chasing a sponsoring director is always done by the planning manager. The Preparer logs in with its own service account, read-only on finance and with write access restricted to the health and agenda fields.

Common mistakes

  • Calculating budget deviation with partial actuals, before the accounting close, and bringing to the meeting a number that changes the following week.
  • Classifying an initiative that was not updated as green; lack of information is not health.
  • Building the agenda in the order of the initiatives list instead of by decision needed, and spending the meeting hearing status on healthy initiatives.
  • Forgetting the decisions from the previous review; the initiative looks new every quarter and the sponsors' commitments disappear.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Initiatives without an update for more than 60 days at closefrom 40% to under 10%estimate based on the described routine
Quarterly review time spent on status instead of decisionsfrom 3 of 4 hours to less than 1 of 2 hoursestimate based on the described routine
Match between the health classification and the team's over the 2 calibration quarters90% or more of initiativesestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Agenda for the Q3 2026 quarterly review, prepared on 2026-10-02. Initiatives: 26. Green 14, yellow 7, red 5. Without an update for more than 60 days: 3.

BLOCK 1, DECISION NEEDED (45 min)
INI-07 New recyclable packaging line | Red | Qualification milestone planned for 2026-08-15, achieved: no; 48 days late | Budget: R$ 6.2 million approved, R$ 7.1 million spent (14.5% deviation) | Pending decision: approve a R$ 1.4 million supplement or rescope | Sponsor: industrial director
INI-19 Northeast distribution center | Red | 2 milestones more than 30 days late | Decision from the previous review (2026-07-03): hire a logistics operator by 2026-08-31, status NOT DONE | Sponsor: supply director
BLOCK 2, ATTENTION (30 min)
INI-03 Shop floor digitalization | Yellow | Milestone 12 days late, budget within band | No pending decision, inform
INI-22 Energy efficiency program | Yellow | No update for 71 days; last narrative from July mentions a supplier being quoted | Action: leader reports before the meeting or the item turns red for lack of information
BLOCK 3, 1 LINE EACH (15 min): 14 green initiatives, listed in the appendix.

Open decisions from previous reviews: 4. Total proposed time: 1 h 30 min instead of 4 h.
